transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but... I came in because for the past few weeks, I've been feeling kind of... well, like there's this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me almost all day. 

I mean, I'm still working and everything! As a nurse, I'm always smiling at my patients and making sure they're okay. But inside, I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together. I'm sorry, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has it been more than two months or less than two months?

Oh, definitely less than two months. It's really only been about... well, maybe three weeks? 

I, um... I feel a little terrible even admitting this out loud, because I know I should just be thrilled, but... it started shortly after I found out I was pregnant. I mean, I know that's supposed to be such wonderful news, and I really *am* thankful, I promise! I just... I don't want you to think I'm a bad person or a bad nurse for feeling so down right now. I hope I'm not sounding awful for saying that. Did I answer your question okay?
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure or interest in activities that you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? I mean, I still love my family and my friends, of course! I really do. But... 

I guess, usually, after my shifts at the clinic, I'd try to do something to decompress, you know? Like, I'd go to a yoga class, or maybe salsa dancing, or even just pull out my paints at home. It was always so nice. But lately... I don't know, I just haven't been doing those things as much. 

Instead, I just kind of... go home and sit on the couch. And sometimes I don't reply to texts right away. It's just... none of it really feels worth the effort right now, I guess? I know that sounds so lazy, and I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise. I just don't have the same energy for it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling like you’re a burden or that you’re failing in your responsibilities, even when others might not see it that way?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely don't want to be a burden to anyone! I try really hard not to be. I still go to work every day, and I make sure my patients are taken care of, and I keep the apartment clean... mostly. 

I guess maybe I feel a little guilty that I'm not, you know, glowing and joyful about the pregnancy like I should be. But I wouldn't say I feel like a failure or a burden. I'm still doing what I'm supposed to do. I really try to pull my weight, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right.
Have you been feeling down or having little interest or pleasure in things almost every day, and does it seem to last most of the day?

Um... well, yes, I suppose so. It's actually kind of why I finally decided to come in. I really tried to just push through it, because I know everyone gets sad sometimes, and I didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But... 

For the past few weeks, I've just had this... this heavy, sad pressure just sitting on me, almost all day long. And it's so silly, because I go to work and I smile at my patients, and I really try to be the cheerful nurse they need! But inside, I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together. It's like I'm just pretending, and it's exhausting. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic, and I really don't mean to complain. I know I have so much to be grateful for. But it is there most of the day, yeah. Am I... am I explaining that okay?
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically or mentally demanding?

Um... no, I don't think so? I mean, I do get tired, of course, but I'm on my feet a lot at the clinic, and... well, with the pregnancy and everything, I think a little fatigue is pretty normal, right? I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining about normal, everyday tiredness! 

If I'm just resting on a day off or haven't done much, I don't feel completely drained or anything like that. I really try to keep my energy up, especially for my patients, so I wouldn't say I have a lack of energy for no reason. I hope that's a good thing? Did I explain that right?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or stay calm? Or have you had any thoughts about not wanting to live or that life isn't worth living?

Um... well, the focus part... I guess maybe a little bit? I really hope it's just from the pregnancy, because I definitely don't want to mess anything up at work. But lately, I've noticed I have to keep rereading medication orders and wound-care notes. It's like my brain just feels kind of foggy, you know? And things I normally do automatically without even thinking... suddenly I just freeze up and second-guess myself. I really try to double-check everything so I don't make mistakes, I promise! 

As for... the other thing you asked... about not wanting to live... oh, no, definitely not! I would never think anything like that. I know how lucky I am, and I really do want to be here for the baby and my patients. I just... I just get a little scrambled sometimes with the decisions. Is that... is that normal for someone in my situation? I really hope I'm not doing a bad job explaining this.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately that seem related to how you’ve been feeling emotionally?

Um... well... I know I really should be eating regularly, especially with the baby and everything. I don't want you to think I'm neglecting that! I always try to make sure I have something. But... I guess lately, food just sounds really unappealing most of the time? 

I'll be halfway through a shift at the clinic, and I'll suddenly realize all I've had all day is just... a few crackers or some coffee. I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible for someone in my condition, and I really am trying to do better! It's just that I don't feel hungry, and eating feels like a chore. I haven't really been tracking my weight because of the pregnancy, but my appetite is definitely... off. 

I hope you don't think I'm a bad mom already for not eating enough. I'm really trying to force myself to eat when I can. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this right now?
Have you been feeling overly guilty or like you’re not good enough, even when things are going okay?

Um... guilty? No, I wouldn't say I feel overly guilty about things. I mean, I definitely want to do my best, especially at the clinic and... and with getting ready for the baby. I try really hard to be a good nurse and a good person, so I don't think I feel like I'm not good enough. 

Sometimes I worry a little bit if I'm doing everything exactly right, but I think that's just because I care so much, you know? I really don't want to let anyone down. But I wouldn't call it guilt, and I definitely don't think I'm worthless or anything like that. I'm just trying to stay positive and do what I'm supposed to do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions okay for you.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual or, on the other hand, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Um... well... I guess I have been a little bit slower lately? I really hope it's just the pregnancy, because I definitely don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or being lazy at work! I try so hard to keep my pace up. But... honestly, everything I do just feels kind of slowed down right now. 

It's almost like I'm moving through syrup, if that makes sense? Even just the really simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound supplies or finishing up my charting... it's taking me noticeably longer than it normally should. I feel terrible about it, and I'm really trying to push through so I don't inconvenience the other nurses or the doctors. I promise I'm still getting all my work done, it just takes a little more effort to get my body to cooperate. 

Is it normal to slow down this much right now? I just want to make sure I'm still doing okay and giving you the right answers.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy level specifically when you're feeling down, even when your physical demands are the same as usual?

Um... well, honestly, I haven't really noticed my energy dropping just because I feel down. I mean, I'm definitely tired, but I think that's just because I'm on my feet all day at the clinic, and... well, being pregnant takes a lot out of you, right? 

I really try my best to keep my energy up, especially for my patients. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm letting my mood affect my work. So, no, I wouldn't say my energy decreases specifically when I'm feeling down... I just get normal-tired from working hard. Does that sound right? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
